A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-DA research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial formatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original commonsense and mathematical reasoning experiments, frozen-A comparisons, training dynamics, rank and component ablations, and an MNIST trajectory study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds LLaMA 2-13B mathematical reasoning results and a Fisher-estimation sample-size study.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 6, changes the displacement estimate from positive to negative inverse-Fisher times gradient, aligning the pseudocode with Equation 21 and correcting the resulting B initialization. This does not establish that the experimental implementation changed. The core initialization objective, K-FAC approximation and LOBPCG solver are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use Commonsense170K and the same eight commonsense benchmarks, MetaMathQA with GSM8K/MATH, and the odd-to-even MNIST scenario. The new model-size and Fisher-sample experiments reuse this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines, including LoRA, PiSSA, MiLoRA, LoRA-One, LoRA-FA and the MNIST full-fine-tuning comparator. The new 13B comparison repeats the existing math-baseline set. DoRA and VeRA are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 13B configuration using Q/K/V adapters and two epochs, alongside the retained 7B configuration using seven projection modules and one epoch. Appendix I adds a controlled Fisher-sample sweep over 16, 64, 256, 1024 and 4096 samples. Existing datasets, metrics and checkpoint-selection procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix I and Table 8 test sensitivity to the number of Fisher-estimation samples, directly examining the default 256-sample budget. Existing component ablations, rank sensitivity and training-dynamics analyses are retained. The MNIST trajectory study moves into Section 5.3 rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, empirical error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new Fisher-sample sensitivity study does not introduce uncertainty estimates for benchmark scores.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes LoRA-One's 7B GSM8K score from 53.8 to 53.7. New Table 3 reports 13B results: LoRA-DA reaches 66.4 on GSM8K and 12.8 on MATH, averaging 39.6 versus PiSSA's 38.9. These are additional settings, not same-setting gains over v1. New Table 8 reports 54.5–55.1 accuracy across Fisher-sample budgets; other matched results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds Auxiliary Lemma C.2 and a derivation of the constrained-MLE variance identity that v1 supported through citations. The Fisher expansion now uses explicit score outer products, and Section 4.3 adds an LOBPCG time-complexity argument. The main initialization bounds and underlying local-distance assumption are retained.

C1.justification: The contribution list explicitly scopes the reported 0.3/1.0 improvements to the 7B model and adds applicability to larger models. It also refines the theoretical contribution from decomposing fine-tuning error to decomposing a bound on expected estimation error. The central Fisher-aware initialization and performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning limited-sample Fisher stability, eigensolver scalability and potential extensions to DoRA and VeRA. Section 5.2 removes v1's broad interpretation that data-aware baselines consistently outperform data-agnostic approaches. The MNIST mechanism explanation is largely retained through relocation.

D1.justification: Table 9 adds model-specific adapter targets and epoch counts for 13B, plus 100 warmup steps alongside the retained 0.03 warmup ratio; their interaction is unexplained. These additions expand reproducibility information without establishing that earlier experiments were rerun. Hardware, other common hyperparameters and the promise to release code upon publication remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Guo et al. (2023), He et al. (2024) and Van der Vaart (2000) to support limited-data Fisher estimation, Fisher–Hessian approximation and MLE asymptotics. The existing related-work survey and positioning against gradient-only initialization are largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected explanatory paragraphs are tightened. MNIST discussion moves into the main text, reproducibility moves to Appendix K, the appendix contents and LLM-usage statement disappear, and an Impact Statement replaces the Ethics Statement. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column presentation with different typography, headers and float arrangements. Figure 3 moves from the appendix into the main text with an expanded caption. Benchmark tables are regrouped, new 13B and Fisher-sensitivity tables are added, and the hyperparameter table gains model-specific rows.

improvement.justification: The 13B comparison and Fisher-sample sweep provide useful additional validation of scalability and the default calibration budget. The corrected pseudocode sign improves implementability, while the added auxiliary derivation makes the variance argument easier to inspect. These are bounded gains to largely retained work; the unexplained coexistence of warmup steps and ratio leaves a small reproducibility ambiguity, and empirical uncertainty reporting remains absent.
